segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello and welcome to Real Easy English, the podcast where we have real conversations in easy English to help you learn.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm Neil.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And I'm Beth. You can find a video version of this podcast and a worksheet to help you learn on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: How are you today, Beth?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I'm okay, Neil. I'm a little bit tired. How are you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm very well. I'm fine. Great.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Good, good. Well, today we're going to talk about mistakes.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So hopefully I won't make many mistakes being tired.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: No, mistakes. Mistakes can be things that are wrong, like a mistake in a maths problem.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But we can also use mistake to talk about really big things in life, decisions that you've made,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: actions that you've taken.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yes, that's true. So I think let's start the conversation.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Let's do it. So Beth, have you made any mistakes recently?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yes. So I recently left my suitcase on a train by mistake.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Oh no

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So I was traveling from home to Leeds on the train and I got to the station at Leeds and there were loads of people and they were football fans and they were singing really loudly and I just wanted to get off the train and that what I did And then I

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: realised about half an hour later that I didn't have my suitcase.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Oh no. That's a bad mistake.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Did you get it back?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I did. I was so lucky. The train stopped at Leeds. So when I realised I ran

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: and said to the people on the platform, my suitcase is on the train. And they held the train for me.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And I ran up the platform. I grabbed my suitcase and then they blew the whistle and the train went.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I was so lucky. But yeah, that was a big mistake. And I will not make that mistake again.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Everybody says that.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: so earlier we said that mistakes can be small things like my suitcase but there are big mistakes

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: that we can make so have you ever made a a big mistake do you think

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: yeah well once um i had a

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: job that i really really enjoyed i was teaching at a school in prague in the czech republic teaching

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: english and i loved the job and i had loads of really good friends but i had this feeling

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: that I needed to go move somewhere else do something else with my life and so I resigned

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: but then about a week or so later I realized I really really didn want to leave that school So I went back to the boss and I said I changed my mind

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I want to stay.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And he said, well, it's too late because I've given your job to somebody else.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Oh, no, that's so sad.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So you left your job, left Prague?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: No, actually, a bit like your suitcase, Beth.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: it ended up being okay because the person who took my job then decided that he didn't want

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: the job either. So in the end, I did stay.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So when we make mistakes, Neil, sometimes we then

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: have a regret or we regret the thing that we did. That means that we feel bad about it or we wish

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: that we'd done something differently.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Do you have any regrets?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, when I was a kid, I guess I was probably 12 or 13,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I had some piano lessons and I quit as soon as I could.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: My parents gave me that choice and I regret that

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: because I love music and I play guitar

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: and I think I would have enjoyed playing piano.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I always think, to be honest, you shouldn't have any regrets because whatever you've done, you've learned something from it.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Even if something bad happened then you know for next time And it a kind of self thing

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: That is a very positive attitude to mistakes Beth

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah, I think it's important to learn from your mistakes.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And that's a common expression in English, to learn from your mistakes.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned in this podcast, starting with mistake.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And a mistake is an action that is wrong or that you do when you don't mean to.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And we can make a mistake. That means we do something wrong.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Or we can do something by mistake, which means we do something accidentally, without meaning to.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: For example, I left my suitcase on the train by mistake.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We also heard regret, which means feel bad or sorry about something you've done or a mistake that you've made.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And we heard learn from your mistakes, which means remember the mistake and then not do it again the next time.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: That's it for this episode of Real Easy English.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: you can test yourself on what you've learned with a worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Next week we'll be talking about trains, buses and public transport.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: See you then. Goodbye.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Bye.
